body.p: Who's on the reindeer? Just the lips! Did he change the tent? He stayed! Who's on the dog? The white-footed one! There'll be no claws left on the white-footed dog. He tied it up. He says: Take off the birch bark! Oh, father, mother, there's no time to tear the mountain ash! Again the crackling came. Again he says: There's no time to defecate and urinate! To those who drink and eat [?]. Having put a bedding under the carcass, they began to remove [untie?], removed. They turned their noses back and forth. This one rushed home on horseback, home. He ran home and crossed the river. He was nowhere near! When he went back to the camp, no one was there. When I went back to the camp, no one was there! "Is the father close?" "He went back to his sons!" "Is the mother close?" "The child's [extra] mouth went backwards! There's no one left. A loon has become a loon. Cliff, cliff! Collapse, collapse! Father, mother, fall down [from the cliff], fall down! Brothers, sisters! Fall down, fall down! Grandma, don't sing! I hit it with a spatula. Where will I find it? Don't sing! A cliff collapsed and crushed my parents. Only one Ostyak left. She crossed the river. Then the bear came and said: "Girl [lit.: father?], where do you cross [the river]? Is it downstream, is it upstream? Here you will not cross! Where do you cross? Is it downstream, is it upstream?" The bear went wading. Cold [wet?] soles, shins, knees, thighs, penis, navel, chest, shoulders, neck, mouth, nose, eyes, head - hid [?]. There: soles made, auntie, ankles; shins made, auntie, - wharf - accept! Excrement let it become, auntie, wants a boat again. Let it become blood - it wants paint. Let it be holes - it wants a scraper, aunty, it wants a scraper! Let it become a hook, auntie! The bucket [invent] wants to become a bucket, let it become a bundle! Auntie, pretty hairs! The child began to live. His brother named Ostyak Ostyak went to fetch water, scooped water with excrement. Did you get water? He poured it out, put the birch bark bast basket, scooped, scooped, poured it out again. We have to spend the night. He lives. Then they came again with others. He's composing a song. Geese, geese! Take me away [lit. lift me up]! The Ostyak takes offence, [I?] would stand with three! Let's finish, let's finish! Ask for swans! Swans, swans! Carry me away! I would stand [i.e. hide?] with three! Swans, swans! Carry me away! I'd stand [i.e. hide] with three [people]! Little one, eh! The orphan cried! Pull out the feathers [lit. armpit feathers?] [for me]! They flew away. And the Ostyak again offended [the orphan]. Sister, pour me some water! I'd stand with three! Brother, brother! Make an onion, make an onion! Will you make an onion? I will! I'll bury my shoes nearby! And again offend [me]! Pour water! They flew away. He stayed behind. He found his grandmother. Grandma, eh! Are you coming? Ogre uncles, come! Where am I going to hide? I'll hide under the needle holder! I put it under the needle. Three men came. Grandma, what have you hidden? Did she look for lice in her shirt? No, no! I know she looked for lice in her shirt! Brother, eh! A woman wants to put her shoes on? Orphan boy is here, he's being abused. Fa, fa, fa, what's it like with women? Brother, eh! Tried the shoe, wanted! She didn't want to try new ones! They spent the night. The next day they got up. They ask again. Children, let's finish! Let our clan fall! They went to hunt sables. The orphan says: Grandma, let me go! I reached the threshold, I crossed the threshold. She let me go. Go the way of your fathers [elders]! He flew, flew, and found it there. They got a wild reindeer, it's freshly killed. Three men, cannibals came. Song. Ogres, ogres [ancestors]! You're up there! Left in advance [lit. to call?]! You left it in the morning [to think/remember?]! You're upstairs! Yeah, what's that you hear? I broke a rib! Ogres, you're upstairs! You've prepared it in advance! To call you in the morning! I can hear it from upstairs. I let the female in. She must fall. He shot him in the little finger. He hurt his little finger. They came back. The mother hid in a hollow tree. They killed and ate. The orphan flew away, there he found Guriwul. Guriwul, Guriwul! A song is close to you! You're thinking of crying! Baba, Baba! Make a bow, make a bow! Will you make an onion? I'll do it! I'll do it in two nights! Just the two of us, just like that! They won't ask! Samoyeds, I have a bow! I have a bowstring! I have a stock of arrows! Baba! Baba! Make a bow, make a bow! Will you make a bow? I will! I'll make one on the mountain! I'll make an iron one! I'll make it in nine [nights]! Yogmak sings: Don't ask! I have the bow! I have a bowstring! I have the stock! Baba, Baba! Make a bow, make a bow! Will you make a bow? I will! I'll make one on the mountain! I'll make an iron one! I'll make it in ten nights! I'll make my own arrows! I'll make arrows with eyes! I'll put earrings in my ears! I can hear songs everywhere! I hear songs everywhere! When the Samoyeds came, he fell down. He began to live, to live, he lived for two years. They had children. When the ogres came, a woman fell down. She stuffed lard into her skin. She killed a reindeer. She pulled the child by the ears - he's crying. When will the brothers come? Why are you crying? He ran away, climbed into his shed, picked up a ladder [the ladder he used to climb up]. He hears a noise. The one is chopping, chopping with his teeth [gnawing]. They have come - already here, close, close! Guriwul, what, close, you say? Earrings in your ears! Across the country [lit. crossing many mountains]! I hear you! I hear! Those two arrows came. They winked and killed two. One left, ran away. Then Guriwul came. He found a broken tooth and put it in his bag. He chased after him and caught up with him. A man is sitting [i.e. living] by the fire. He stepped over their fire - burned the meat, (and) they laugh. They are laughing themselves. Guriwul understood. Let's go to the people! Look for lice! Am I going to look for lice? Guriwul looked for lice. Man, what do you want? It's itchy, it's lice! He took a tooth from his pouch, took it and jabbed it into the back of his head and he died. People, bring a pillow! He's sleeping at his uncle's place! The end.
